We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 5 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <=9999 (we cannot check price but assume). Need to construct JSON route.

We have target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We have some templates that break ester to give precursor with carboxylic acid? The apply_template with template 1037371 gave precursor: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](OC(=O)/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)[C@H]1C)CO". That's a huge molecule with two ester groups? Actually seems to add a protecting group? Not good.

Maybe simpler: The target looks like a dihydroxy cyclohexane with a side chain containing conjugated diene and a terminal carboxylic acid (maybe a fatty acid). Could be derived from simpler fragments: a cyclohexane diol (maybe from shikimic acid) and a side chain (C=C-C=C-COOH). Could use esterification of a hydroxy group with a carboxylic acid.

We could break the ester (C(O)=O) attached to the side chain? Actually the target has a terminal carboxylic acid (C(O)=O) attached to a conjugated diene chain. The side chain also has an internal hydroxyl? The SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Interpret: a cyclohexane ring with two OH groups (one external O attached to side chain). The side chain: O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C is an ether linking to the ring? Actually O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C is an allylic alcohol? Hard.

Maybe we can propose a route: start from shikimic acid (commercial) which is similar to cyclohexene triol with carboxylic acid. Shikimic acid SMILES: OC1C(O)C(O)C(=O)C=C1O? Actually shikimic acid is C7H10O5, SMILES: O=C(O)C1C(O)C(O)C=CC1O. That matches part of our target? Our target has a cyclohexane with two OH and an ether side chain. Could be derived from shikimic acid via protection and coupling.

We need leaves commercially available: shikimic acid is buyable. Also maybe 3-methyl-2-buten-1-ol (prenol) or similar for side chain. The side chain is a conjugated diene with terminal COOH: maybe sorbic acid (trans, trans-2,4-hexadienoic acid) SMILES: C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O. That's commercially available. Indeed sorbic acid is C6H8O2, SMILES: C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O. That matches the side chain after the ether? The target has O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C? Actually there is a CO group (CH2OH) attached to the diene? The side chain includes a CH2OH at the first double bond? The SMILES: /C=C(CO)/C indicates a double bond with a CH2OH substituent. So side chain is 3-hydroxy-2-methyl-2-butenyl? Not exactly.

Maybe we can break the ether linking the side chain to the cyclohexane, giving two fragments: cyclohexane diol (maybe shikimic acid derivative) and a side chain alcohol (maybe 3-hydroxy-2-methyl-2-butenoic acid). Could use SN2 or Mitsunobu.

Simplify: propose retrosynthesis:

Step 1: Disconnection of ether O between cyclohexane OH and side chain: use SN2 alkylation of cyclohexanol with side chain bromide.

So precursors: cyclohexane diol (maybe 1,3-dihydroxycyclohexane) and side chain bromide (e.g., 3-bromo-2-methyl-2-buten-1-ol). Both could be buyable.

Check buyability: let's test cyclohexane-1,3-diol SMILES: C1CC(O)C(O)C1. We already checked it's buyable True.

Now side chain: 3-bromo-2-methyl-2-buten-1-ol SMILES? Let's construct: C=C(CO)CBr? Actually need bromine attached to carbon that will link to O. The side chain in target is O-CH- (attached to cyclohexane) then CH (attached to cyclohexane) then /C=C(CO)/C (a double bond with CH2OH substituent). So the side chain fragment after cleavage would be something like CH(Br)-C(=C(CO)C)?? Might be complex.

Alternative: Use ester formation: the terminal carboxylic acid could be formed by oxidation of an alcohol side chain. So we could have side chain alcohol (C/C=C/C=C/CO) which is 5-hexen-1-ol with conjugated diene? Actually 5-hexen-1-ol with double bonds: C/C=C/C=C/CO (SMILES). Check buyability: let's test.
